title: Two Pakistani nationals arrested in Karnataka for allegedly creating fake voter IDs and ration cards
summary: In Karnataka, two Pakistani nationals, Farah Naz and Mohammad Fardeen, were arrested on charges of allegedly creating fake voter IDs and ration cards. The incident has raised concerns about the security of voter registration and identity documents in the state.
summary_points: Two Pakistani nationals were arrested in Karnataka for alleged creation of fake voter IDs and ration cards
The arrests have sparked concerns about voter registration and identity document security in the state
Karnataka has a large population of migrant workers from Pakistan, raising questions about their integration into Indian society

center: Centrist coverage frames the story as a law enforcement issue, focusing on the arrests and charges against the two Pakistani nationals. However, some outlets also touch upon the broader implications for migrant workers and voter registration security.

केंद्रीय समाचार संगठन मतपुलिसी मामले को एक कानून प्रवर्तन मुद्दा के रूप में फोकस करते हैं, दो पाकिस्तानी नागरिकों पर आरोप लगाते हैं। हालांकि, कुछ समाचार संगठन मतगिरने वालों और मतदाता पंजीकरण सुरक्षा के बारे में भी संकेत करते हैं।
